```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
has_pdftools <- requireNamespace("pdftools", quietly = TRUE)
```

bodybuildr was written for one job: the CIM immunization country profile.
That profile is a navy banner, section headers with an orange tick, rules-only
tables with status icons, legends and grey placeholder panels on US Letter.

This vignette checks whether the package is general or just that profile
under a new name. It builds three documents that share nothing with the
profile: no navy, no orange, no Letter-portrait grid, and all data random.

| Document | Page | Look | What it stresses |
|---|---|---|---|
| **HALCYON-7 telemetry** | 11 × 8.5 in landscape, 2 pp | Dark dashboard, gradient banner, mono type | Custom blocks (KPI tiles, sparklines, meters), blocks inside table cells, flexible rows |
| **The Fermentation Almanac** | US Letter, 2 pp | Cream paper, serif, newspaper masthead | Editorial typography, inline runs, masonry layout, data-frame tables, page-dependent header |
| **Nightjar festival passes** | 4 × 6 in, 3 pp | Gradient per attendee | Tiny page size, `header = function(ctx)`, per-page data, images from arrays |

Every page below is written by `export_pdf()` and turned into PNGs with
pdftools so it can be shown here. No height on any page was typed by hand
unless the code says so.

```{r packages}
library(bodybuildr)
library(grid)
library(ggplot2)
set.seed(7)

out_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "bodybuildr-showcase")
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Use a nice installed font when there is one, a generic family otherwise.
font_or <- function(want, fallback) {
  fams <- unique(systemfonts::system_fonts()$family)
  hit <- want[want %in% fams]
  if (length(hit)) hit[1] else fallback
}

# Export, then show every page as an image.
show_pdf <- function(doc, name, dpi = 110) {
  file <- export_pdf(doc, file.path(out_dir, paste0(name, ".pdf")))
  if (!has_pdftools || !isTRUE(getOption("knitr.in.progress"))) return(message("Written to ", file))
  n <- pdftools::pdf_info(file)$pages
  # knitr's figure path, so the HTML embeds the images and knitr cleans them up
  pngs <- vapply(seq_len(n), function(i) knitr::fig_path(".png", number = i), character(1))
  dir.create(dirname(pngs[1]), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  pdftools::pdf_convert(file, dpi = dpi, filenames = pngs, verbose = FALSE)
  knitr::include_graphics(pngs)
}

`%|NA|%` <- function(a, b) ifelse(is.na(a), b, a)
```

## Custom blocks

The country profile only ever used built-in blocks. A dashboard needs pieces
the package doesn't ship, so the first test is how hard it is to add one.
`new_block()` asks for two functions: `measure(width)` returns a height and
`render(width, height)` returns a grob. Once a custom block has those, it can
go in stacks, columns, boxes and table cells like any built-in one.

```{r custom-blocks}
# Height of one line in a theme text style, in inches.
line_in <- function(style, role = "body") {
  gp <- text_gpar(style, role)
  gp$fontsize * gp$lineheight / 72
}

# A theme colour by name, or the colour itself.
theme_col <- function(x) bb_get_theme()$colors[[x]] %||% x

# 1. A horizontal rule. bodybuildr has no built-in rule block.
hrule <- function(color = "ink", lwd = 1, lty = "solid") {
  new_block("hrule",
    measure = function(width) lwd / 96,
    render = function(width, height) {
      segmentsGrob(0, 0.5, 1, 0.5,
                   gp = gpar(col = theme_col(color), lwd = lwd, lty = lty, lineend = "butt"))
    })
}

# 2. A KPI tile: label, delta, big value, sparkline. Its height comes from the
#    theme's text sizes, so it follows any theme change.
kpi_tile <- function(label, value, delta, series, good = "up") {
  lab_st <- text_style("small", case = "upper", weight = 700)
  val_st <- text_style(size = 22, weight = 700)
  dlt_st <- text_style("small", weight = 700)
  spark_h <- 0.32; gap <- 0.05
  new_block("kpi",
    measure = function(width) line_in(lab_st) + gap + line_in(val_st) + gap + spark_h,
    render = function(width, height) {
      th <- bb_get_theme()
      up <- delta >= 0
      ok <- if (good == "up") up else !up
      dgp <- text_gpar(dlt_st); dgp$col <- th$status[[if (ok) "yes" else "no"]]
      y2 <- line_in(lab_st) + gap + line_in(val_st)
      top <- function(y) unit(1, "npc") - unit(y, "in")
      xs <- (seq_along(series) - 1) / (length(series) - 1)
      ys <- (series - min(series)) / max(diff(range(series)), 1e-9)
      gTree(children = gList(
        # text_gpar() carries font, size and colour, but not `case`
        textGrob(toupper(label), 0, top(0), just = c("left", "top"), gp = text_gpar(lab_st)),
        textGrob(sprintf("%s%.1f%%", if (up) "▲ " else "▼ ", abs(delta)),
                 unit(1, "npc"), top(0), just = c("right", "top"), gp = dgp),
        textGrob(value, 0, top(y2), just = c("left", "bottom"), gp = text_gpar(val_st)),
        gTree(vp = viewport(y = 0, height = unit(spark_h, "in"), just = "bottom"), children = gList(
          polygonGrob(c(xs, 1, 0), c(ys, 0, 0),
                      gp = gpar(fill = adjustcolor(th$colors$primary, 0.15), col = NA)),
          linesGrob(xs, ys, gp = gpar(col = th$colors$primary, lwd = 1.4)),
          pointsGrob(1, ys[length(ys)], pch = 19, size = unit(3, "pt"),
                     gp = gpar(col = th$colors$accent))))
      ))
    })
}

# 3. A progress meter, meant for table cells.
meter <- function(frac, color = "primary", height = 0.08) {
  frac <- max(0, min(1, frac))
  new_block("meter",
    measure = function(width) height,
    render = function(width, height) gTree(children = gList(
      roundrectGrob(r = unit(height / 2, "in"), gp = gpar(fill = theme_col("rule_light"), col = NA)),
      roundrectGrob(x = 0, width = unit(frac, "npc"), just = "left", r = unit(height / 2, "in"),
                    gp = gpar(fill = theme_col(color), col = NA)))))
}

measure_block(kpi_tile("Test", "42", 1, 1:5), width = 2)
```

## 1. HALCYON-7: a dark, landscape ops dashboard

### Theme and template

The theme overrides the palette names the built-in components draw with
(`panel`, `rule_strong`, `on_primary`, ...), so the section headers, legends
and grid tables from the profile turn dark without any other change. It also
adds a new colour (`void`) and a new text role (`mono`).

```{r ops-theme}
sans <- font_or(c("Avenir Next", "Helvetica Neue", "Helvetica"), "sans")
mono <- font_or(c("Menlo", "Courier New"), "mono")

ops_theme <- bb_theme(
  font = sans, base_size = 8.5,
  colors = list(void = "#0B0F1A", panel = "#141B2D", panel_alt = "#1A2236",
                ink = "#E6EAF2", text2 = "#B8C0D2", muted = "#8892A6", faint = "#5C677D",
                primary = "#7AE7C7", accent = "#FF5D8F", on_primary = "#FFFFFF",
                on_primary_muted = "#D9CCF5", rule_strong = "#2E3A55", rule_light = "#232C42",
                rule_faint = "#1C2438"),
  text = list(section = text_style(size = 10, weight = 700, color = "primary", case = "upper"),
              table_header = text_style(color = "void", weight = 700, case = "upper"),
              footer = text_style(family = mono, size = 7, color = "faint"),
              mono = text_style(family = mono, size = 7.5, color = "text2")),
  status = c(yes = "#3DDC97", no = "#FF4D6D", unknown = "#5C677D")
)
```

The banner logo is not a file. It is a ringed planet built as an RGBA array,
which `bb_banner()` accepts directly.

```{r ops-template}
planet <- local({
  n <- 240
  g <- expand.grid(x = seq(-1, 1, length.out = n), y = seq(-1, 1, length.out = n))
  r <- sqrt(g$x^2 + g$y^2)
  shade <- pmin(1, pmax(0, 0.35 + 0.65 * (1 - sqrt((g$x + 0.45)^2 + (g$y - 0.45)^2) / 1.6)))
  u <- g$x * cos(0.4) + g$y * sin(0.4); v <- -g$x * sin(0.4) + g$y * cos(0.4)
  e <- sqrt(u^2 + (v / 0.28)^2)
  ring <- e > 0.78 & e < 0.98 & !(r <= 0.62 & v > 0)
  a <- array(0, c(n, n, 4))
  a[, , 1] <- matrix(0.48 * shade + 0.5 * ring, n)
  a[, , 2] <- matrix(0.91 * shade, n)
  a[, , 3] <- matrix(0.78 * shade + 0.3 * ring, n)
  a[, , 4] <- matrix(as.numeric(r <= 0.62 | ring), n)
  pmin(a, 1)
})

ops_tpl <- page_template(
  width = 11, height = 8.5, margin_x = 0.45, margin_top = 0.35, margin_bottom = 0.3,
  theme = ops_theme, background = "void", header_gap = 0.22, footer_gap = 0.15,
  header = bb_banner(
    "HALCYON-7  //  WEEKLY TELEMETRY", "Deep-space probe operations brief (fictional data)",
    logo = planet,
    style = banner_style(fill = gradient_fill(c("#121735", "#3A1C71", "#D76D77")),
                         height = 0.95, logo_height = 0.62, accent_color = "primary",
                         accent_height = 0.03,
                         title_style = text_style("title", size = 20, family = mono))),
  footer = bb_page_footer("MISSION ELAPSED SOL {sol}  ·  DSN PASS {pass}", "PAGE {page}/{pages}",
                          style = footer_line_style(rule = line_style("rule_strong", 1)))
)

# Section header: same function as in the profile, restyled into a flat pill.
sec <- function(x, refs = NULL) bb_section_header(x, refs = refs, style = section_header_style(
  marker_color = "accent", marker_width = 0.12, marker_height = 0.04,
  rule = line_style("rule_strong", 0.75)))

panel <- function(x) bb_box(x, box_style(fill = "panel", radius = 0.06, padding = 0.14))
```

### Content

```{r ops-content}
walk <- function(n, start, sd) start + cumsum(rnorm(n, 0, sd))
kpis <- bb_cols(
  panel(kpi_tile("Distance from Sun", "4.82 AU", 1.9, walk(30, 4.6, 0.01))),
  panel(kpi_tile("Downlink rate", "11.4 kbps", -6.2, walk(30, 12, 0.4))),
  panel(kpi_tile("Battery SoC", "87%", 2.4, walk(30, 84, 0.6))),
  panel(kpi_tile("Hull temperature", "-142 °C", 3.1, walk(30, -145, 0.5), good = "down")),
  panel(kpi_tile("Science frames", "2,318", 14.0, cumsum(rpois(30, 75)))),
  gap = 0.14
)

dark_gg <- theme_minimal(base_family = sans, base_size = 8) + theme(
  plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#141B2D", colour = NA),
  panel.grid = element_line(colour = "#232C42", linewidth = 0.3),
  text = element_text(colour = "#B8C0D2"), axis.text = element_text(colour = "#8892A6"),
  legend.position = "bottom", plot.margin = margin(8, 10, 6, 6),
  plot.title = element_text(colour = "#E6EAF2", face = "bold", size = 9))

t <- seq(0, 5.2 * pi, length.out = 400)
traj <- data.frame(x = (0.3 + t / 6) * cos(t), y = (0.3 + t / 6) * sin(t),
                   phase = cut(t, 4, labels = c("Launch", "Cruise", "Flyby", "Science")))
bodies <- data.frame(x = c(0, 1.1, -2.2, 3.2), y = c(0, 0.4, -1.4, 0.9),
                     name = c("Sun", "Earth", "Mars", "Jupiter"), s = c(5, 2, 1.6, 3.5))
traj_plot <- ggplot(traj, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_path(aes(colour = phase), linewidth = 0.9, lineend = "round") +
  geom_point(data = bodies, aes(size = s), colour = "#E6EAF2", show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(data = bodies, aes(label = name), colour = "#8892A6", vjust = -1.2, size = 2.4, family = sans) +
  annotate("point", x = tail(traj$x, 1), y = tail(traj$y, 1), colour = "#FF5D8F", size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#5C677D", "#7AE7C7", "#D76D77", "#FFD166"), name = NULL) +
  scale_size_identity() + coord_equal() +
  labs(title = "Heliocentric trajectory", x = NULL, y = NULL) + dark_gg

# Table cells hold blocks: a status icon, a custom meter, a styled cell().
subsys <- data.frame(
  name = c("Power (RTG)", "Attitude control", "High-gain antenna", "Thermal", "Propulsion", "Star tracker B"),
  state = c("yes", "yes", "no", "yes", NA, "yes"),
  load = runif(6, 0.25, 0.95))
sub_tbl <- bb_table(
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(subsys)), function(i) list(
    subsys$name[i],
    bb_status(subsys$state[i], size = 0.12),
    meter(subsys$load[i], if (subsys$load[i] > 0.85) "accent" else "primary"),
    cell(sprintf("%d%%", round(100 * subsys$load[i])), style = "mono"))),
  header = c("Subsystem", "OK", "Load", ""),
  widths = unit(c(1, 0.35, 1.1, 0.4), c("null", "in", "in", "in")),
  align = c("left", "center", "left", "right"),
  style = table_style_grid(fill = "panel", alt_fill = "panel_alt", header_fill = "primary",
                           border = line_style("rule_strong", 0.5),
                           divider = line_style("rule_strong", 0.5), pad_x = 0.06, pad_y = 0.055))

status_legend <- bb_legend(list(
  legend_key("status", "Nominal", state = "yes"), legend_key("status", "Fault", state = "no"),
  legend_key("status", "No telemetry", state = "unknown"), legend_key("swatch", "Load > 85%", "accent")))

days <- c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")
hm <- expand.grid(hour = 0:23, day = factor(days, levels = rev(days)))
hm$frames <- rpois(nrow(hm), lambda = 6 + 10 * exp(-((hm$hour - 14)^2) / 18))
heat <- ggplot(hm, aes(hour, day, fill = frames)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "#141B2D", linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#1A2236", high = "#7AE7C7", name = "frames / h") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 21, 3), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(title = "Instrument duty cycle", x = "UTC hour", y = NULL) + dark_gg +
  theme(legend.key.height = unit(5, "pt"), legend.key.width = unit(28, "pt"),
        panel.grid = element_blank())

anomalies <- data.frame(
  t = sprintf("SOL %d %02d:%02d", 1420 + sort(sample(0:3, 5, TRUE)), sample(0:23, 5), sample(0:59, 5)),
  sev = c("accent", "#FFD166", "primary", "accent", "#FFD166"),
  msg = c("HGA pointing error 0.42° > limit; safed to LGA",
          "Star tracker B stray light, 3 frames dropped",
          "Reaction wheel 2 momentum dump (planned)",
          "Bus undervoltage transient 27.1 V for 40 ms",
          "Thermal margin on IR detector < 2 K"))
anom_tbl <- bb_table(
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(anomalies)), function(i) list(
    bb_dot(anomalies$sev[i], size = 0.09), cell(anomalies$t[i], style = "mono"), anomalies$msg[i])),
  widths = unit(c(0.18, 1.3, 1), c("in", "in", "null")), align = c("center", "left", "left"),
  style = table_style(divider = line_style("rule_strong", 0.5), pad_y = 0.05, valign = "top"))
```

### Page 1: flexible rows

Each plot sits in a row next to a table. A plot without a height is
flexible, so it stretches to the height of its tallest sibling. A row with a
fixed sibling is itself fixed, though, so any page height left over goes
unused.

The fix stays inside the layout model. A `bb_spacer()` at the end of the
right-hand stack makes that stack flexible. Every child of the second row is
then flexible, so the row takes the page's leftover height and the heatmap
grows into it.

```{r ops-page1}
ops_page1 <- bb_page(
  kpis,
  bb_cols(
    panel(bb_plot(traj_plot, min_height = 1.95)),
    bb_stack(sec("Subsystems", refs = "live"), sub_tbl, status_legend, gap = 0.08),
    widths = unit(c(1, 4.1), c("null", "in")), gap = 0.2),
  bb_cols(
    panel(bb_plot(heat, min_height = 1.5)),
    bb_stack(sec("Anomaly log", refs = "72 h"), anom_tbl,
             bb_legend(list(legend_key("dot", "Critical", "accent"),
                            legend_key("dot", "Warning", "#FFD166"),
                            legend_key("dot", "Info", "primary"))),
             bb_spacer(),                       # <- makes the whole row flexible
             gap = c(0.06, 0.06, 0)),
    widths = unit(c(1, 4.1), c("null", "in")), gap = 0.2),
  template = ops_tpl, gap = 0.18, data = list(sol = 1423, pass = "DSS-43")
)
```

### Page 2: synced tables and a placeholder

```{r ops-page2}
instruments <- data.frame(
  code = c("IRS", "MAG", "UVS", "PLS", "CAM-N", "CAM-W", "RSS", "DUST"),
  name = c("Infrared spectrometer", "Magnetometer", "UV spectrograph", "Plasma analyser",
           "Narrow-angle camera", "Wide-angle camera", "Radio science", "Dust counter"),
  team = c("JPL / Pasadena", "IC / London", "LASP / Boulder", "SwRI / San Antonio",
           "MSSS / San Diego", "MSSS / San Diego", "DLR / Cologne", "MPI / Heidelberg"),
  gb = round(rexp(8, 1 / 40), 1))

volume_dots <- function(gb) {
  k <- min(5, ceiling(gb / 20))
  bb_dot(c(rep("primary", k), rep("rule_strong", 5 - k)), size = 0.07, gap = 0.025)
}
inst_tbl <- bb_table(
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(instruments)), function(i) list(
    cell(instruments$code[i], style = text_style(family = mono, weight = 700, color = "primary")),
    paste0(instruments$name[i], "\n", span(instruments$team[i], color = "muted", size = 7)),
    volume_dots(instruments$gb[i]),
    cell(sprintf("%.1f GB", instruments$gb[i]), style = "mono"))),
  header = c("ID", "Instrument", "Volume", ""), header_case = "upper",
  widths = unit(c(0.6, 1, 0.6, 0.6), c("in", "null", "in", "in")),
  align = c("left", "left", "left", "right"),
  style = table_style(divider = line_style("rule_strong", 0.5), header_rule = line_style("primary", 1)))

uplink <- sample(c("yes", "yes", "yes", "no", NA), nrow(instruments), TRUE)
plan_tbl <- bb_table(
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(instruments)), function(i) list(
    sample(c("Survey", "Calibrate", "Stare", "Idle", "Raster scan"), 1),
    bb_status(uplink[i], size = 0.1,
              label = c(yes = "Approved", no = "Rejected")[uplink[i]] %|NA|% "Pending"))),
  header = c("Next week", "Uplink"), header_case = "upper",
  style = table_style(divider = line_style("rule_strong", 0.5), header_rule = line_style("primary", 1)))

ops_page2 <- bb_page(
  sec("Instrument roster & next uplink", refs = "sync_rows = TRUE"),
  # two-line rows on the left; sync_rows makes the right table's rows match
  bb_cols(inst_tbl, plan_tbl, widths = c(2.4, 1), gap = 0.3, sync_rows = TRUE),
  bb_cols(
    bb_placeholder("Spectrometer cube downlink scheduled for SOL 1426. Nothing to show yet.",
                   fill = stripe_fill(c("panel", "panel_alt"), angle = 30, width = 0.12),
                   label_fill = "void", style = text_style("placeholder", color = "muted")),
    panel(bb_stack(
      bb_text("Flight director note", style = text_style("subheading", color = "accent")),
      bb_text(paste0("The **HGA fault** on SOL 1421 cost one DSN pass. ",
                     "Mitigation: re-point with star tracker A only, accept **0.1°** extra jitter.\n\n",
                     "- Raise IR detector heater set-point by 1.5 K\n",
                     "- Defer dust counter calibration\n- Request extra 70 m pass"),
              markup = "markdown", style = "note"),
      gap = 0.06)),
    widths = c(1, 1), gap = 0.2),
  template = ops_tpl, gap = c(0.06, 0.25), data = list(sol = 1423, pass = "DSS-43")
)
```

```{r ops-show, out.width = "100%", echo = FALSE}
show_pdf(bb_document(ops_page1, ops_page2), "halcyon-7")
```

## 2. The Fermentation Almanac: a serif magazine

This one goes the other way: warm paper, Georgia, italic section heads with
no marker, and a newspaper masthead. There is no banner here. The masthead
is a stack of rules (the custom `hrule()`) and centred text.

```{r alm-theme}
serif <- font_or(c("Georgia", "PT Serif", "Times New Roman"), "serif")
alm_theme <- bb_theme(
  font = serif, base_size = 9.5,
  colors = list(paper = "#F6F0E4", ink = "#2B2118", text2 = "#4A3B2C", muted = "#7C6A55",
                faint = "#A8977F", primary = "#7A2E1F", accent = "#C8963E", panel = "#EDE3CF",
                panel_alt = "#E4D7BE", rule_strong = "#2B2118", rule_light = "#CDBF9F",
                rule_faint = "#DDD2BA"),
  text = list(body = text_style(lineheight = 1.5),
              section = text_style(size = 13, weight = 400, italic = TRUE, color = "primary"),
              kicker = text_style(size = 7.5, weight = 700, color = "accent", case = "upper"),
              quote = text_style(size = 15, italic = TRUE, color = "primary", lineheight = 1.3),
              table_header = text_style(size = 7.5, weight = 700, color = "ink"),
              footer = text_style(size = 7.5, italic = TRUE, color = "muted")),
  status = c(yes = "#5C7A3A", no = "#7A2E1F", unknown = "#A8977F"))

alm_sec <- function(x, refs = NULL) bb_section_header(x, refs = refs, style = section_header_style(
  marker_color = NA, rule = line_style("rule_light", 0.75), space_below = 0.06))

# The running header is a function of the page: none on the cover page.
alm_tpl <- page_template(
  margin_x = 0.7, margin_top = 0.55, margin_bottom = 0.5, theme = alm_theme, background = "paper",
  header = function(ctx) if (ctx$page == 1) NULL else
    bb_running_header("The Fermentation Almanac", "Vol. III · No. 9",
                      style = header_line_style(
                        left_style = text_style(italic = TRUE, color = "ink", weight = 400),
                        rule = line_style("ink", 0.6))),
  footer = bb_page_footer("Printed on paper that was once a tree", "— {page} —",
                          style = footer_line_style(rule = NULL)),
  header_gap = 0.25)
```

```{r alm-content}
lorem <- function(n) {
  w <- c("brine", "lactic", "crock", "salt", "cabbage", "weight", "bubbles", "cellar", "patience",
         "sour", "garlic", "dill", "kahm", "yeast", "starter", "jar", "rind", "koji", "miso", "whey",
         "temperature", "the", "of", "and", "a", "slowly", "every", "morning", "under", "with", "until")
  s <- paste(sample(w, n, TRUE), collapse = " ")
  paste0(toupper(substr(s, 1, 1)), substr(s, 2, nchar(s)), ".")
}
para <- function(k) paste(replicate(k, lorem(sample(9:16, 1))), collapse = " ")

masthead <- bb_stack(
  hrule("ink", 2.5), bb_spacer(0.03), hrule("ink", 0.6),
  bb_text("The Fermentation Almanac", align = "center",
          style = text_style(size = 38, weight = 700, lineheight = 1.1)),
  bb_cols(bb_text("Vol. III · No. 9", style = "kicker"),
          bb_text("Autumn, being the season of crocks & brine", align = "center",
                  style = text_style("note", italic = TRUE)),
          bb_text("Price: one sourdough starter", align = "right", style = "kicker"),
          widths = c(1, 2, 1), valign = "center"),
  hrule("ink", 0.6), bb_spacer(0.03), hrule("ink", 2.5),
  gap = 0.06)

# Pull quote: a box around a flexible spacer is a flexible coloured bar,
# so in a row it stretches to the height of the quote next to it.
pull_quote <- bb_cols(
  bb_box(bb_spacer(), box_style(fill = "accent")),
  bb_stack(bb_text("“Salt is a clock. Two percent tells time in weeks; five percent, in seasons.”",
                   style = "quote"),
           bb_text("— Old cellar proverb, probably invented", style = text_style("small", italic = TRUE)),
           gap = 0.06),
  widths = unit(c(0.05, 1), c("in", "null")), gap = 0.14)

ph <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("Sauerkraut", "Kimchi", "Dill pickles"), function(k) {
  d <- 0:21; k0 <- runif(1, 0.15, 0.35)
  data.frame(day = d, ph = 3.3 + 3 * exp(-k0 * d) + rnorm(22, 0, 0.04), batch = k)
}))
ph_plot <- ggplot(ph, aes(day, ph, linetype = batch, colour = batch)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 4.6, colour = "#7A2E1F", linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
  annotate("text", x = 21, y = 4.7, label = "safe below 4.6", hjust = 1, family = serif,
           size = 2.6, colour = "#7A2E1F", fontface = "italic") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#2B2118", "#C8963E", "#7A2E1F")) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("solid", "longdash", "dotdash")) +
  labs(x = "Day", y = "pH") + theme_classic(base_family = serif, base_size = 8) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#F6F0E4", colour = NA),
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#F6F0E4", colour = NA))
# The legend is a bodybuildr block, not ggplot's.
ph_legend <- bb_legend(list(legend_key("line", "Sauerkraut", "#2B2118"),
                            legend_key("dash", "Kimchi", "#C8963E"),
                            legend_key("line", "Dill pickles", "#7A2E1F")),
                       note = "n = 1 crock each")

recipe <- bb_table(
  list(list("Green cabbage", "1.0 kg", "100%"),
       list(cell("cored, shredded fine", style = text_style("small", italic = TRUE), indent = 0.15), "", ""),
       list("Sea salt (no iodine)", "20 g", "2%"),
       list("Caraway seed", "4 g", "0.4%"),
       list("Juniper berries", "6", cell("to taste", style = text_style(color = "faint", italic = TRUE))),
       list(cell("**Total**", markup = "markdown"), cell("1.03 kg", style = text_style(weight = 700)), "")),
  header = c("Ingredient", "Qty", "Baker's %"), header_case = "upper",
  widths = c(2.4, 1, 1.3), align = c("left", "right", "right"),
  style = table_style(header_rule = line_style("ink", 1.2), divider = line_style("rule_light", 0.5),
                      pad_y = 0.045))

suitability <- bb_table(
  list(list("Vegan", bb_status("yes", size = 0.11)),
       list("Gluten-free", bb_status("yes", size = 0.11)),
       list("Low sodium", bb_status("no", size = 0.11)),
       list("Kid-approved", bb_status(NA, size = 0.11)),
       list("Difficulty", bb_dot(c("primary", "primary", "rule_light"), shape = "diamond", size = 0.1))),
  widths = c(2, 1), align = c("left", "right"),
  style = table_style(divider = line_style("rule_light", 0.5), pad_y = 0.04, last_divider = FALSE))

alm_page1 <- bb_page(
  masthead,
  bb_cols(
    bb_stack(bb_text("Feature", style = "kicker"),
             bb_text("Two percent, forever", style = text_style(size = 22, weight = 700, lineheight = 1.1)),
             bb_text(para(4)), pull_quote, bb_text(para(3)), gap = 0.1),
    bb_stack(bb_text("Dispatch", style = "kicker"),
             bb_text("Letters from the cellar", style = text_style(size = 15, weight = 700, lineheight = 1.15)),
             bb_text(paste0(span("Q. ", weight = 700, color = "primary"), lorem(14), "\n",
                            span("A. ", weight = 700, color = "accent"), para(2))),
             bb_text(paste0(span("Q. ", weight = 700, color = "primary"), lorem(10), "\n",
                            span("A. ", weight = 700, color = "accent"), para(1))),
             bb_box(bb_text(paste0("Write to us: ", link("https://example.org/almanac", "example.org/almanac")),
                            style = "note", link_color = "primary"),
                    box_style(border = line_style("ink", 0.6, lty = "22"), padding = 0.08)),
             gap = 0.1),
    widths = c(1.6, 1), gap = 0.3),
  alm_sec("The acid curve", refs = "fig. 1"),
  bb_cols(bb_stack(bb_plot(ph_plot, height = 1.9), ph_legend, gap = 0.02),
          bb_stack(bb_text("Recipe card", style = "kicker"), recipe, bb_spacer(0.08),
                   bb_text("Suitability", style = "kicker"), suitability, gap = 0.05),
          widths = c(1.25, 1), gap = 0.3),
  template = alm_tpl, gap = c(0.25, 0.25, 0.04)
)
```

### Page 2: masonry classifieds

There is no grid component. Three independent `bb_stack()`s in a `bb_cols()`
give a masonry layout, because every ad measures its own height from its
text.

```{r alm-page2}
ad_styles <- list(
  box_style(border = line_style("ink", 0.8), padding = 0.1),
  box_style(fill = "panel", padding = 0.1),
  box_style(border = line_style("ink", 0.8, lty = "22"), padding = 0.1),
  box_style(fill = "ink", padding = 0.1),
  box_style(border = line_style("primary", 1.5), radius = 0.08, padding = 0.1))
titles <- c("Crocks wanted", "Starter seeks discard", "Lost: kombucha SCOBY", "Brine therapy",
            "Koji lessons", "Weights for hire", "Cellar to let", "Pickle swap", "Miso of the month",
            "Free whey", "Airlock repair", "Honest sauerkraut")
ads <- lapply(seq_along(titles), function(i) {
  st <- ad_styles[[(i - 1) %% length(ad_styles) + 1]]
  inverse <- identical(st$fill, "ink")
  bb_box(bb_stack(
    bb_text(titles[i], style = text_style(weight = 700, case = "upper", size = 8.5,
                                          color = if (inverse) "paper" else "ink")),
    bb_text(lorem(sample(8:30, 1)), style = text_style("note", color = if (inverse) "panel" else "text2")),
    gap = 0.04), st)
})
col_of <- rep_len(1:3, length(ads))
masonry <- bb_cols(.list = lapply(1:3, function(k) bb_stack(.list = ads[col_of == k], gap = 0.12)),
                   gap = 0.15)

alm_page2 <- bb_page(
  alm_sec("Classifieds", refs = "masonry: three independent stacks"),
  masonry,
  bb_placeholder("Your advertisement here. Rates on request; payment accepted in jars.",
                 fill = stripe_fill(c("paper", "panel"), angle = 60, width = 0.06), height = 0.9,
                 style = text_style("placeholder", italic = TRUE), label_fill = "paper"),
  alm_sec("Almanac table", refs = "data.frame in, table out"),
  bb_table(data.frame(Month = month.abb[9:12],
                      `Cellar °C` = sprintf("%.1f", runif(4, 9, 16)),
                      `Best for` = c("Cucumbers", "Cabbage & roots", "Miso, doenjang", "Citrus preserves"),
                      Moon = c("Waxing", "Full", "Waning", "New"), check.names = FALSE),
           widths = c(1, 1, 2.5, 1), align = c("left", "right", "left", "left"), header_case = "upper",
           style = table_style_grid(header_fill = "ink", alt_fill = "panel", fill = "paper",
                                    header_style = text_style("table_header", color = "paper"),
                                    border = line_style("ink", 0.6), divider = line_style("rule_light", 0.5))),
  bb_spacer(),   # pushes the colophon to the bottom of the body
  bb_text("Colophon: every height on this page was measured, none typed.",
          align = "center", style = text_style("small", italic = TRUE)),
  template = alm_tpl, gap = c(0.04, 0.2, 0.25, 0.04, 0, 0)
)
```

```{r alm-show, out.width = "100%", echo = FALSE}
show_pdf(bb_document(alm_page1, alm_page2), "almanac")
```

## 3. Nightjar: 4 × 6 in festival passes

The last document is a small page with one page per attendee. The banner
colours change per page, so the header is a `function(ctx)` that reads the
page's `data`. The QR-like code is a random matrix scaled up into an image
array.

```{r fest}
display <- font_or(c("Futura", "Avenir Next", "Helvetica Neue"), "sans")
fest_theme <- bb_theme(
  font = display, base_size = 8,
  colors = list(ink = "#16112B", muted = "#6B6585", rule_light = "#E3DFF0", panel = "#F3F0FA",
                panel_alt = "#E6E0F5", on_primary = "#FFFFFF", on_primary_muted = "#FFFFFFCC"),
  text = list(title = text_style(size = 22, weight = 700, case = "upper"),
              subtitle = text_style(size = 9, case = "upper"),
              table_header = text_style(size = 6.5, weight = 700, color = "muted", case = "upper"),
              footer = text_style(size = 6.5, color = "muted")))

qr <- function(seed, n = 25, scale = 10) {
  set.seed(seed)
  m <- matrix(rbinom(n * n, 1, 0.5), n)
  finder <- function(m, r, c) {
    m[r:(r + 6), c:(c + 6)] <- 1; m[(r + 1):(r + 5), (c + 1):(c + 5)] <- 0
    m[(r + 2):(r + 4), (c + 2):(c + 4)] <- 1; m
  }
  m <- finder(finder(finder(m, 1, 1), 1, n - 6), n - 6, 1)
  big <- kronecker(1 - m, matrix(1, scale, scale))
  array(rep(big, 3), c(dim(big), 3))
}

passes <- data.frame(
  name = c("Ada Okonkwo", "Mateo Ríos-Villanueva", "Yuki Tanaka"),
  tier = c("Artist", "Weekend", "Crew"),
  hue1 = c("#FF6B6B", "#4D96FF", "#6BCB77"), hue2 = c("#845EC2", "#16112B", "#0F4C5C"),
  stages = c(3, 2, 4), serial = sprintf("NJ-%05d", c(90408, 28727, 51130)))
zones <- c(Main = "#FF6B6B", Forest = "#6BCB77", Lake = "#4D96FF", Backstage = "#16112B")

fest_tpl <- page_template(
  width = 4, height = 6, margin_x = 0.25, margin_top = 0.2, margin_bottom = 0.18, theme = fest_theme,
  header = function(ctx) bb_banner(
    "Nightjar", paste(ctx$data$tier, "pass · 12–14 June"),
    style = banner_style(fill = gradient_fill(c(ctx$data$hue1, ctx$data$hue2), dir = "tlbr"),
                         height = 1.0, divider = NULL, accent_color = NA)),
  footer = bb_page_footer("No. {serial}", "{page} of {pages}"),
  header_gap = 0.18, footer_gap = 0.1)

fest_pages <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(passes)), function(i) {
  p <- passes[i, ]
  allowed <- names(zones)[seq_len(p$stages)]
  bb_page(
    bb_text(p$name, style = text_style(size = 17, weight = 700, lineheight = 1.05)),
    bb_cols(
      bb_image(qr(i)),
      bb_table(list(list("Gate", c("Lake", "South", "North")[i]),
                    list("Camping", bb_status(i != 2, size = 0.1)),
                    list("Lockers", bb_status(NA, size = 0.1)),
                    list("Zones", bb_dot(zones[allowed], size = 0.1, shape = "square"))),
               header = c("Access", ""), widths = c(1, 1), align = c("left", "right"),
               style = table_style(pad_y = 0.04, divider = line_style("rule_light", 0.5))),
      widths = c(1, 1.2), gap = 0.18, valign = "center"),
    bb_legend(Map(function(z, col) legend_key("swatch", z, col), names(zones), zones),
              key_size = 0.1, gap = 0.12),
    bb_spacer(),   # tear-off stub sits on the footer
    bb_box(bb_cols(bb_text("Drink token ×3", style = text_style(weight = 700, case = "upper")),
                   bb_text("tear here", align = "right", style = text_style("small", italic = TRUE)),
                   valign = "center"),
           box_style(fill = stripe_fill(c("panel", "panel_alt"), angle = 135, width = 0.05),
                     border = line_style("muted", 0.8, lty = "22"), padding = c(0.1, 0.12), radius = 0.06)),
    template = fest_tpl, gap = c(0.12, 0.12, 0, 0),
    data = list(serial = p$serial, tier = p$tier, hue1 = p$hue1, hue2 = p$hue2))
})
```

```{r fest-show, out.width = "32%", echo = FALSE}
show_pdf(bb_document(.list = fest_pages), "nightjar")
```

## Verdict: how generic is it?

**Very generic in layout, less so in drawing primitives.** All three
documents were built without changing the package. Every piece written for
the country profile took on a different job:

| Profile component | Reused here as |
|---|---|
| `bb_banner()` | Gradient mission header with an array logo; per-attendee festival header |
| `bb_section_header()` | Flat pill marker on dark; italic, marker-less magazine heads |
| `bb_table()` + `bb_status()` | Subsystem board with custom meters; recipe card; access list on a ticket |
| `bb_legend()` | Line/dash legend for a ggplot; zone swatches |
| `bb_placeholder()` | "Downlink pending" panel; classified-ad slot |
| `sync_rows = TRUE` | Instrument roster with two-line rows next to a plan table |
| `page_template()` tokens | `{sol}`, `{pass}`, `{serial}`, not just `{country}` |

**What held up well**

- *The layout model.* Masonry, flexible rows, a flexible accent bar and a
  bottom-pinned tear-off stub all came from `bb_stack()`, `bb_cols()` and
  `bb_spacer()`. No coordinates were needed.
- *Themes.* Overriding the palette names flipped every built-in component to
  dark or sepia. Custom colours (`void`, `paper`) and roles (`mono`,
  `kicker`, `quote`) can be used by name anywhere.
- *Extensibility.* A KPI tile with a sparkline takes about 30 lines with
  `new_block()`, and it works in boxes, rows and table cells straight away.
- *Page sizes.* Landscape, Letter and 4 × 6 in all work with nothing
  special.

**Friction found while building this** (candidates for the package):

1. **No horizontal-rule block.** Mastheads and dividers needed the 8-line
   `hrule()` above. A `bb_rule(line_style())` would be cheap to add.
2. **`text_gpar()` drops `case`.** Custom blocks have to call `toupper()`
   themselves.
3. **No public colour resolver.** `.col()` is internal, so custom blocks use
   `bb_get_theme()$colors[[x]] %||% x`. Exporting something like
   `theme_color()` would help.
4. **A row is fixed if any child is fixed.** Leftover page height doesn't
   reach a plot that sits next to a table. The `bb_spacer()` trick works, but
   you have to know it. `page_layout()` also counts flexible blocks at their
   minimum height, so it reports "free" space that render will actually
   fill.
5. **No flow or pagination.** Text doesn't flow between magazine columns (the
   paragraphs were split by hand). A long table doesn't break across pages:
   `export_pdf()` only warns about overflow.
6. **Tables have no `colspan`/`rowspan`**, and there is no rotated text.
7. **ggplot doesn't inherit the theme.** Fonts and colours were repeated in
   `dark_gg` and `theme_classic(...)`. A `bb_gg_theme()` bridge would remove
   that duplication.
8. **The banner has a single layout** (logos | divider | title/subtitle) and
   doesn't fill `{tokens}`. A `function(ctx)` header gets around that.
9. **Fixed vocabularies.** `bb_status()` only knows yes/no/unknown, and legend
   keys are a closed set of six types.
10. **One page size per export.** Mixed sizes need separate PDFs.
11. **Custom text roles don't travel.** A block using `style = "kicker"`
    fails with "Unknown text role" under any theme that lacks that role. There's
    no fallback to a default role.

None of these stopped a design. Each needed a few lines of user code or a
layout trick, and the core block contract (`measure`/`render`) never got in
the way.
